issues.failure_explanation: The lower bound in EQN:xbound fails for lattice points with |hλ| < h·rad(V_0): the midpoint hλ/2 lies in V_{hλ} (faces are removed from V_0) and satisfies |hλ/2| < h·rad(V_0) − |hλ| whenever |hλ| < (2/3)h·rad(V_0), e.g. Λ = Z^d, d ≥ 4, λ = e_1 at x = e_1/2. Moreover, even where the pointwise bound holds, |x|^p ≥ ||hλ| − rad||^p does not imply ∫|x|^p dμ ≥ ||hλ|^p − rad^p|·μ(V_{hλ}); the claimed integral inequality is false: for Λ = Z, h = 1, p = 2, μ = δ_{0.51}, one has 0.51^2 = 0.2601 < |1 − 1/4|·1 = 0.75. The statement (i) itself is false: the same example gives LHS = |1|^2·1 = 1 but RHS = (1/2)^2 + 0.51^2 = 0.5101 < 1.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the constant 1 in (i) by 2^{p−1}: from |hλ| ≤ |x| + h·rad(V_0) for x ∈ V_{hλ} and (a+b)^p ≤ 2^{p−1}(a^p+b^p), summing gives ∑_λ |hλ|^p μ(V_{hλ}) ≤ 2^{p−1}(h^p rad(V_0)^p + M_p(μ)); the two downstream finiteness proofs go through with the same constant and no advertised rate changes.
issues.overall_effect: The moment-finiteness steps of Theorems THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac and THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant (the only places item (i) is used) rely on the false inequality; the approximation-rate conclusions are unaffected once (i) is repaired.
issues.title: Lemma LEM:RadialEstimates item (i) is false and its proof's lower bound for |x| on V_{hλ} is invalid
issues.why_classification: A one-line constant repair fixes the lemma and both downstream finiteness arguments; every advertised rate, regime, and conclusion is preserved, so the repair is short, local, and routine.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: let $\mc{N}(K,T)$ be the minimal number of translates of $T$ it takes to cover $K$, i.e., $\mc{N}(K,T) = \min\{\#(\alpha_i)\subset\R^d:K \subset \bigcup_i T+\alpha_i\}.$
The Voronoi cells tile the space by translation, i.e., $\R^d=\cup_{\lambda\in\Lambda}V_0+\lambda$.

Let $N\in\N$ be fixed, $\mc{N}=\mc{N}(B_R,V_0)$, and set $h=3\left(\frac{\mc{N}}{N}\right)^{\frac1d}$. Then $\mu_h = \sum_{\lambda\in \Lambda} \mu(V_{h\lambda})\delta_{h\lambda}$ is an at most $N$-term approximation of $\mu$

issues.failure_explanation: The lattice cells meeting B_R themselves form a cover of B_R by translates of hV_0, so their number is at least the covering number N(B_R, hV_0), not at most it; the proof's first inequality is backwards. The true term count is #{hλ : hλ ∈ B_{R + h·rad(V_0)}}, which can vastly exceed N = 3^d h^{−d} N(B_R, V_0): e.g. Λ = 1000Z × Z^99 ⊂ R^100 (so V_0 = [−500,500]×[−1/2,1/2]^99, rad(V_0) ≈ 500), R = 1, μ uniform on B_{0.1}, and N = 3^100·N(B_1,V_0) (giving h = 1). Then N(B_1,V_0) ≤ 3^99, hence N ≤ 3^199 ≈ 10^95, but the number of terms is #{k ∈ Z^99 : |k| ≤ 500} ≈ |B_500^99| ≈ 10^228 ≫ N. The statement also omits the hypothesis h ≤ 1 (equivalently N ≥ 3^d N(B_R,V_0)) needed for Lemma LEM:CoveringNumber and Theorem THM:InfiniteLatticeDirac.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redefine the covering number on an enlarged ball: with R' = R + diam(V_0), every cell meeting B_R lies in B_{R'}, so the term count is at most N(B_{R'}, hV_0) ≤ 3^d h^{−d} N(B_{R'}, V_0); setting h = 3(N(B_{R'},V_0)/N)^{1/d} with N ≥ 3^d N(B_{R'},V_0) restores the at-most-N-terms conclusion with the same rate 3·rad(V_0)·N(B_{R'},V_0)^{1/d}·N^{−1/d}.
issues.overall_effect: The N-term guarantee of THM:NTermDirac and of its N-term corollaries (COR:NTermPiecewiseConstant, COR:NpixelDirac, COR:NpixelIndicator, and cor:added-1) is unsupported and, as shown, false for the stated parameters; the O(N^{−1/d}) rate itself survives only after reparameterizing the covering number.
issues.title: THM:NTermDirac: the 'at most N-term' count uses the covering number in the wrong direction and is false in general
issues.why_classification: The stated N-term guarantee is false and cannot be retained with N(B_R,V_0); the repair is a contained reparameterization (enlarged ball in the covering number) that keeps the method and the O(N^{−1/d}) rate, so it needs no new proof architecture but does modify the theorem's parameters.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $f_\mu(x) \leq \frac{\eps^p}{ 3C \vert x \vert^{p+d+1} }$ where $C$ is the integration constant from integrating over concentric $d$-spheres,

issues.failure_explanation: Since ∫_{r≥R} r^{d−1}/r^{d+1} dr = ∫_R^∞ r^{−2} dr = 1/R, the displayed estimate only yields I_1 ≤ ε^p/(3R), which is ≤ ε^p/3 only when R ≥ 1. The theorem never assumes R ≥ 1, so for R < 1 hypothesis (1) does not deliver the required ε^p/3 budget for the absolutely continuous part; an omitted hypothesis is needed.

failure_location.quote: I_1 &= \int_{B_R^c} \big( \vert x \vert - R \big)^p f_\mu(x) dx \leq \frac{\eps^p}{3C } \int_{B_R^c} \underbrace{\frac{\big( \vert x \vert - R \big)^p}{\vert x \vert^{p}}}_{< 1} \frac{1}{\vert x \vert^{d+1}} dx < \frac{\eps^p}{3 } \underbrace{\int_{r \geq R} \frac{r^{d-1}}{r^{d+1}} dr}_{\leq 1} \leq \frac{\eps^p}{3}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis R ≥ 1, or absorb the factor 1/R into hypothesis (1) by replacing the denominator 3C|x|^{p+d+1} with 3C·max{1,R}·|x|^{p+d+1}; either one-line change makes the displayed bound valid for all R > 0.
issues.overall_effect: For radii R < 1 the conclusion W_p(μ, μ̂) < ε is unestablished; the corollary cor:added-1 inherits the gap.
issues.title: THM:noncompact_ext: the I_1 estimate silently requires R ≥ 1
issues.why_classification: A single local condition (or constant adjustment) repairs the estimate with no change to the method, the conclusion, or the advertised scope.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Then $W_p(\mu, \widehat{\mu}) < \eps$, where $\widehat{\mu}$ is the compactly supported measure ${(P_{B_R})}_\sharp \mu$.

issues.failure_explanation: With a = ⌊R⌋ + 1 − R ∈ (0,1], ∑_{j≥⌊R⌋} (j+1−R)^{−2} = ∑_{k≥0} (a+k)^{−2} ≥ ∑_{k≥0}(1+k)^{−2} = π^2/6, with equality only for integer R; the sum is unbounded as a → 0^+ (R approaching an integer from below). So the underbraced bound ≤ π^2/6 is false in general, and hypothesis (2) only yields I_2 ≤ (ε^p/3)(6/π^2)S(R) with S(R) > π^2/6 for non-integer R. The conclusion is actually false, not merely unproved: for R = 0.95, p = 1, ε = 10^{−3}, take μ = μ_⊥ uniform on the sphere |x| = 0.99; hypothesis (2) holds since μ_⊥(B_{(0,1]}) = 1 ≤ (10^{−3}/(3·0.05^3))·(6/π^2) ≈ 1.62, yet W_1(μ, μ̂) ≥ |0.99 − 0.95| = 0.04 > ε. (For integer R the same computation also drops the annulus (R, R+1) in the displayed decomposition, though the following inequality still dominates it.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Retune hypothesis (2): replace the factor 6/π^2 by (∑_{j≥⌊R⌋}(j+1−R)^{−2})^{−1}, or restrict the theorem to integer R; the existing proof then closes and the 'suitable decay ⇒ W_p(μ, μ̂) < ε' scope is preserved.
issues.overall_effect: The noncompact extension theorem fails for non-integer R under its stated hypotheses, and the N-term corollary cor:added-1, which builds on it, is unreliable in that regime.
issues.title: THM:noncompact_ext: the annulus series bound is reversed, so hypothesis (2) does not imply I_2 ≤ ε^p/3 and the conclusion is false for non-integer R
issues.why_classification: The statement is false as written and the decay hypothesis must be strengthened (or R restricted); this is a contained re-tuning of one constant rather than new proof architecture, and the advertised scope survives in weakened form.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Let $\mu\in W_p(\R^d)$, $p\in[1,\infty)$ have compact support contained in the interior of $B_R$.
In particular, the measure $\pi(\R^d, B) = \widehat{\mu}(B)$ is supported entirely on the ball $B_R$.

issues.failure_explanation: μ̂ = (P_{B_R})_# μ is supported on the closed ball B̄_R (mass outside B_R is projected onto ∂B_R), whereas THM:NTermDirac and COR:NTermPiecewiseConstant require the support to lie in the interior of B_R. The N-term bounds in the corollary therefore do not follow from those theorems as stated; the invoked results are used outside their hypotheses.

failure_location.quote: Since $\widehat{\mu}$ is compactly supported within some ball of radius $R$, we have by \Cref{THM:NTermDirac} and \Cref{THM:LatticePiecewiseConstant} that $W_p(\widehat{\mu},\widehat\mu_h)\leq 3 \rad(V_0) \mathcal{N}^{\frac{1}{d}} N^{-\frac{1}{d}}$ and $W_p(\widehat\mu,\widehat\mu_h') \leq 3 \diam(V_0) \mathcal{N}^{\frac{1}{d}} N^{-\frac{1}{d}}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Apply the N-term theorems with a slightly enlarged radius R' = R + δ (δ > 0), so supp(μ̂) ⊂ int B_{R'}; the same bounds hold with N(B_{R'}, V_0) in place of N(B_R, V_0).
issues.overall_effect: The two N-term estimates in cor:added-1 are unsupported as stated, independently of the corollary's reliance on the defective noncompact theorem and the term-count issue.
issues.title: cor:added-1: the N-term theorems are applied to μ̂ supported on the closed ball, violating their interior-support hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Enlarging the ball is a routine local fix that restores the invoked theorems' hypotheses with no change to the method or the rate.
